```python
def f(inputs: List[Tuple[int, int]]):
    '''
    inputs: a list of tuples, where each tuple contains two integers
    '''

    # XOR operation on two integers will always give an odd result, 
    # except when we have the same numbers whose binary representation has even number of '1's. 
    # Better way to understand this - XOR operation gives us a value that keeps changing if two bits are different.
    # Moreover, when two integers differ only in last bit, they will have an even XOR value. 
    # If we XOR the two same numbers, we will get 0. 
    # Requested result is the XOR operation on signature points. To get a minimized result form, 
    # we first need to sort the signatures and then find XOR of 1st and last signature,
    # XOR of 2nd and 2nd last, XOR of 3rd and 3rd last, so on and so forth.

    # We take advantage of pythonic simple sort and easy to follow `zip` to get the final result.
    sigs = sorted(inputs)

    # By calculating final XOR result, we will get the minimized signature pattern in the end.
    # Python have no in-build exor property on list, so we perform XOR calculation over all numbers in list.
    return sum(x ^ y for x, y in zip(sigs, sigs[::-1])) 
```

Our task is simple, we just return XOR over all signature points for maximized distinction between two points.

The time complexity depends on the sorting of the list as XOR of already sorted can be done in O(N). The space complexity is also O(1) because we're not using more space than required.
